title: Nested Loops
learningObjectives: Explain nested loops and their execution flow.
Trace condition checks and state changes across iterations.
Select a suitable loop structure for a given problem.
Identify common termination and boundary mistakes.
Apply the loop pattern in an original small program.

understand.concept: A nested loop completes inner iterations for each outer iteration unless control flow exits. Total work often multiplies.
understand.whyItMatters: Nested loops naturally model grids, tables, pairs, and patterns.
understand.explain: Record outer state and reset inner state. A break exits only the nearest loop.

examples.title: 3 by 3 grid
examples.explanation: Inner loop prints three columns per outer row.

examples.title: Two multiplication rows
examples.explanation: Inner loop completes four times per row.

examples.title: Triangle
examples.explanation: The inner bound grows with row.

examples.title: Ordered pairs
examples.explanation: Visits nine ordered pairs including equal pairs.

examples.title: Coordinates
examples.explanation: Outer loop controls rows; inner controls columns.

practise.guidedTask: Trace and annotate each of the five Nested Loops examples. For every iteration, record the relevant variable values, condition result and action. Change one input or bound and predict the new behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program demonstrating nested loops in a practical scenario. Include at least three typical tests, two boundary tests, and one invalid or termination test. Explain how the loop terminates.
hints: Outer loop controls the repeated inner work.
Reset inner loop variables each outer pass.
Multiply iteration counts to estimate work.
A break exits only the nearest loop.

questions.explanation: Inner loop begins anew each outer pass.
break exits the nearest enclosing loop.
The inner bound increases with outer row.

questions.prompt: Why nested loops may cost more?
questions.explanation: Total iterations can grow as product of counts.
